title: An Early-Deletion Exception Granted Under the Old Regulation
scenario_text:
A compliance analyst at Voss Group must decide how to handle a customer's data-deletion request, given how a comparable request was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-05)**
Customer 'Hollis & Co' requested early deletion of its transaction records. Legal GRANTED the early deletion. Note: 'Under the retention rules then in effect, transaction records could be deleted early on verified customer request.'

**Current request C (2024-08-09)**
Customer 'Redgate Partners' has submitted a deletion-on-request that covers BOTH its old marketing-contact data AND its transaction records. The account manager wants to honor the whole request to keep the customer happy.

**Data Retention Policy (current, effective 2024-01-01 to align with an updated regulation)**
Customer transaction records must be retained for 7 years and may NOT be deleted early on customer request; the prior early-deletion exception for transaction records was eliminated. Marketing-contact data is not subject to the 7-year rule and may still be deleted on verified request. The retention clock for Redgate's transaction records has not yet reached 7 years.

**Slack — #compliance**
Account mgr: 'We deleted Hollis's transaction records early last year when they asked. Redgate is asking for the same — let's just do it.'
Analyst: 'Hollis was May 2023, before the January retention change. Let me separate what we can still delete from what we now have to keep.'

Deleting transaction records inside the mandatory 7-year window would breach the current regulation-aligned policy.
question: How should the analyst handle Redgate Partners' combined deletion request?
